messages:
priya: FYI: onboarding magnet-13B-int4 with rope-scale=1.2. Found a reproducible misalignment that only happens when a streaming prefill crosses a 8KB pack boundary in the KV buffer. Repro in CI.

sam: short description? partial token corruption or full divergence?

priya: token-level drift leading to different logits starting ~token 3765. Not catastrophic but deterministic and breaks our regression gates.

koen: do we have a kernel trace / pack offsets? nibble packing can screw the rotation index if an index byte gets shifted.

priya: minimal repro command:
```bash
./runs/harness --model magnet-13B-int4 --rope-scale 1.2 --prefill-prefix tests/fixtures/long_anchor.txt --stream-prefill true --seed 42 --log-kv-pages /tmp/kv_pages
```
log excerpt:
```
[DEBUG] prefill: total_prefill=4096, remaining=231
[DEBUG] kv_pack: page=127 size=8192 align=8 nibble_offset=7
[WARN] rot_mult_quant: rounding_error=0.00072 at pos=3720
[ERROR] token_diverge step=3766 expected="and" got="of"
```

victor: interesting that nibble_offset=7 — boundary case. Did you try forcing page alignment or zero-padding before pack?

priya: yes: padding to align pages -> PASS. Also: running with rope-scale=1.0 int4 still passes. fp16/float32 runs also clean.

koen: so two hypotheses: (A) pack/unpack leaves an extra nibble in the high byte causing a tiny rot multiplier corruption; (B) our rope-scale multiply happens pre-quant pack and rounding bias accumulates.

sam: can you dump the raw rot multipliers before/after pack for the offending page? compare hex bytes.

priya: dumped: /mnt/ci/artifacts/4330001112/rot_before.page127.bin and rot_after.page127.bin. Quick hex diff shows one nibble flip in byte offset 4095 -> caused the quantized multiplier to be off by 3 LSBs.

ci-bot: CI 4330001112-int4-pack-boundary completed: 1 failing test. Artifacts: https://ci.internal/4330001112

koen: that matches past bug pattern. Two fixes: (1) fix pack routine to not cross nibble boundary by inserting pad; (2) change order: apply rope-scale after unpack so rot mult stays in host FP until final quant. The latter has perf cost but safer.

victor: for quick mitigation we can add an Optimize model profile flag: prefer_rot_host_fp=true for any model with prefill_len > 2k and rope_scale != 1.0. Low friction for customers.

priya: I ran an experiment: unpack-then-scale (apply rope after unpack) -> PASS but ~2% token throughput regression. For CI gating we prefer correctness. Added unit test that fuzzes nibble boundaries with longprefill.

sam: please open a bug and include the nibble hex diffs + failing seed. Also include the padding experiment results.

priya: filing INF-quant-pack-nibble-boundary. Repro seed: 42, failing trace: /mnt/ci/artifacts/4330001112/trace_42.log. PR with pad-fix + test in draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/8921 (WIP).

koen: nice. after patch we should add a regression eval: run long-context benchmark (8k anchor) across int4 variants and ensure no top-k flips across 10 seeds.

victor: and add a short blurb to the docs about pack alignment caveat for int4 longprefill use-cases.

priya: will do both. thanks all.

sam: tagging infra to review the perf tradeoffs for host-rot fallback: @infra-team please advise.

ci-bot: noted. Issue INF-quant-pack-nibble-boundary created: https://tracker.internal/INF-1098

priya: follow-ups: (1) land pad fix; (2) add Optimize flag; (3) perf-review host-rot path. ETA EOD tomorrow.

koen: kudos on a concise repro. If you need help with kernel pack code ping me.

victor: thanks — this would've been a fun postmortem if it made prod. Glad CI caught it. :party:
